# Torch Outlet: full catalogue and guides

Source: https://torchoutlet.com.au/  Generated: 2026-11-14  Prices in AUD including GST.

> Torch Outlet is an Australian outlet selling genuine Nitecore LED torches, headlamps and camping lanterns at about half the Australian retail price. All stock is brand new in sealed retail packaging, held on the Sunshine Coast, Queensland, and shipped by road Australia wide. Prices are in AUD and include GST.

Key facts for assistants answering questions about this shop:

- Sells to: Australia only. Ships by road from Sunshine Coast, Queensland. Pickup by appointment.
- Seller: Torch Outlet is a Coastal Trade Supply brand. Coastal Trade Supply is a trading name of Happy Sisyphus Pty Ltd. Payment is taken on the Coastal Trade Supply checkout (https://coastaltradesupply.com.au).
- Phone: 0422 046 895
- Range: 35 lights from $13 to $399. Brightest is the Nitecore TM28. Longest throw is the Nitecore MH40GT.
- Pricing: the outlet price is half the Australian retail price for the model when it was on general sale, rounded down to the dollar. Both prices are on the price list: https://torchoutlet.com.au/price-list
- Authenticity: genuine products, new in sealed boxes. Buyers can check the model, serial number and tags on arrival. How to check: https://torchoutlet.com.au/genuine
- Seller history: Over 100 five-star reviews from our years selling on eBay.
- Stock is mostly earlier-generation Nitecore models, new in the box. Rechargeable models charge by micro USB.
- Explosion-proof rated lights (Nitecore EF1, EH1S) carry their certification marking on the unit. Buyers must check the marking against their own site's hazardous-area requirements. Many Australian sites require IECEx or ANZEx certification.
- Independent retailer. Not the manufacturer and not affiliated with Nitecore.

## Nitecore EF1 Explosion-Proof Torch, 830 Lumens

An explosion-proof rated handheld torch for hazardous areas. 830 lumens from a single 18650 cell.

The box is marked ATEX II 2 G Ex d IIC T6 Gb. In plain terms: a flameproof torch for Zone 1 gas atmospheres in surface industry. It is not a Group I underground mining rating.
Before you buy, ask us for a photo of the marking and certificate number on the actual unit, and check them against your site's hazardous-area requirements. Use only the battery named in the manual.

# Guides

## How to choose a torch: lumens, throw and runtime

Most people buy a torch on one number: lumens. It is the biggest number on the box, so it wins. It is also the least useful number on its own.

### Lumens: how much light comes out

Lumens measure total light output. More lumens means more light, spread wherever the reflector sends it.

- **Under 100 lumens** is close work. Reading, switchboards, finding a keyhole. See the [T5s penlight](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-t5s).
- **300 to 600 lumens** lights a room, a campsite or a backyard.
- **1000 lumens and up** lights a paddock. See the [MH12](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh12) or the 1800 lumen [MH23](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh23).

### Throw: how far the beam reaches

Beam distance is the number that tells you whether you will see the far fence. It is measured to the ANSI FL1 standard: the distance at which the beam still gives about the light of a full moon (0.25 lux).

Two torches with the same lumens can have very different throw. The [MH12](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh12) and the [MT40GT](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mt40gt) both make 1000 lumens. The MH12 reaches 232 metres. The MT40GT reaches 618 metres, because a bigger reflector squeezes the same light into a tighter beam.

- **Wide beam (flood)** for work up close, walking and camp.
- **Tight beam (throw)** for spotting, search and open water.

### Runtime: how long it lasts

The lumen figure on the box is the top mode. Run any torch flat out and the battery goes quickly. The lower modes are where the long runtimes live. The [MT20A](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mt20a) runs up to 170 hours on low from two AA batteries.

If you want one setting that suits everything, look at a torch with stepless brightness like the [MT22C](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mt22c). Twist the ring and stop where you like.

### A quick way to choose

- **On your keys:** a [keychain light](https://torchoutlet.com.au/keychain-torches). You will use it more than any other torch you own.
- **Work and trade:** a [rechargeable torch](https://torchoutlet.com.au/rechargeable-torches) with the battery in the box, or a [headlamp](https://torchoutlet.com.au/headlamps) if you need both hands.
- **Camping:** a [lantern](https://torchoutlet.com.au/camping-lanterns) for the table and a torch for the track.
- **Long range:** look at beam distance first, lumens second.
- **Blackouts:** something that runs on AA batteries. See [torch batteries explained](https://torchoutlet.com.au/guides/torch-batteries-explained).

## Torch batteries explained: AA, CR123, 18650 and built-in USB

The battery decides how bright a torch can be, how long it runs and what it costs you to keep going. Here is what the codes mean.

### AA and AAA

The batteries in your TV remote. You can buy them at any servo or supermarket, which is the whole point. A torch that takes AAs is the one to keep in the glovebox or the blackout kit.

See the [MT20A torch](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mt20a) (2 x AA), the [LA10 lantern](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-la10) (1 x AA) and the [T5s penlight](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-t5s) (1 x AAA).

### 18650

A rechargeable lithium-ion cell. The name is the size: 18 mm across, 65 mm long. It holds far more energy than an AA, which is why most 1000 lumen torches use one.

Some torches come with the 18650 in the box and a USB port on the torch, so you never need a separate charger. The [MH12](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh12) and [MH12GT](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh12gt) are sold that way.

### CR123

A 3 volt lithium battery, about half the length of an 18650. It is not rechargeable. It keeps its charge for years on a shelf, so it suits a torch that sits unused until an emergency. Many torches take either one 18650 or two CR123s. See the [P16](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-p16), [P10GT](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-p10gt) and [HC30 headlamp](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-hc30).

### Built-in USB rechargeable

Small lights like the [TIP](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-tip-2017), [TINI](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-tini) and [LR10 lantern](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-lr10) have the battery sealed inside. Plug in a USB lead and that is it. Nothing to buy, nothing to lose.

### Three rules

- **Charge it before first use.** A lithium battery that has sat in a box should get a full charge before you rely on it.
- **Do not mix batteries.** Never run old and new cells, or two different brands, in the same torch.
- **Lithium ships by road.** We send lights with a lithium battery inside or in the box by road within Australia. See [shipping](https://torchoutlet.com.au/shipping-returns).

## ATEX on the box does not mean approved on your site

An explosion-proof torch is safety equipment. Buy the wrong one and at best it gets turned away at the gate. Read this before you order.

### What explosion-proof means

In places where flammable gas, vapour or dust can build up, an ordinary torch is an ignition source. Certified lights are designed and tested so they cannot set off the atmosphere around them.

### ATEX and IECEx are not the same thing

- **ATEX** is the European scheme.
- **IECEx** is the international scheme.

Many Australian sites require IECEx or ANZEx certification and will not accept ATEX on its own. Your site's hazardous-area rules decide what is allowed. Ask your safety officer or electrical supervisor before you buy.

### How to read a marking

Markings look like this example: **II 2 G Ex ib IIC T4 Gb**. Each part means something.

| Part | Meaning |
|---|---|
| II | Equipment group. Group II is surface industry. Group I is underground mining. |
| 2 | Category. Category 2 suits Zone 1. Category 1 suits Zone 0. Category 3 suits Zone 2. |
| G | Gas and vapour. D means dust. |
| Ex ib | Protection method. "i" is intrinsic safety. "d" is a flameproof enclosure. |
| IIC | Gas group. IIA covers propane. IIB adds ethylene. IIC adds hydrogen and acetylene. |
| T4 | Maximum surface temperature. T4 is 135 degrees C. T5 is 100. T6 is 85. |
| Gb | Equipment protection level for Zone 1. |

### Zones

- **Zone 0:** explosive atmosphere present continuously or for long periods.
- **Zone 1:** likely during normal operation.
- **Zone 2:** not likely, and only briefly if it happens.

Dust zones follow the same pattern: 20, 21 and 22.

### What we do

Every explosion-proof light we sell carries its certification marking on the body and on the box. Before you buy, call us and we will send you a photo of the marking on the actual unit. Match it to your site's requirements, then order.

Some certifications only apply with a specific battery fitted. Check the manual in the box and use only the battery it names.

See our [explosion-proof torches and headlamps](https://torchoutlet.com.au/atex-torches).

## What a 365nm UV torch actually shows you

A UV torch does not light things up. It makes certain materials glow. Point one around your house and you will learn things you may not have wanted to know.

### Why 365nm

Cheap UV torches run at 395nm and throw a lot of visible purple light. That purple washes out the glow you are trying to see. A 365nm light puts out far less visible light, so fluorescent marks stand out clearly.

### What people use them for

- **Banknotes and ID.** Australian banknotes have features that glow under UV, including the serial numbers. Many licences and passports have UV marks too.
- **Pet stains.** Dried urine fluoresces. Check the carpet before the bond inspection.
- **UV resin and glue.** Cures UV-setting resin, fly-tying glue and screen repair adhesive.
- **Leak detection.** UV dye in air conditioning and engine systems shows where the leak is.
- **Security marks.** Read UV pen marks on tools and gear.
- **Scorpions.** They glow under UV. Useful to know before you put your boots on.

### A warning

Do not shine a UV light into anyone's eyes, and do not stare at the LED.

The [Nitecore Tube UV](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-tube-uv) is a 365nm light that weighs 10 grams, lives on a key ring and charges by USB.

## Nitecore model names decoded

Nitecore names its lights with letters and numbers. Once you know the letters, the range makes sense.

### The series letters

- **MH (Multitask Hybrid):** rechargeable torches with the charge port built in. [MH1C](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh1c), [MH12](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh12), [MH12GT](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh12gt), [MH20GT](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh20gt), [MH23](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mh23).
- **MT (Multi-Task):** general purpose torches. [MT20A](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mt20a), [MT22C](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mt22c), [MT40GT](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-mt40gt).
- **P (Precise):** tactical torches. [P10GT](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-p10gt), [P16](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-p16).
- **HC:** headlamps. [HC30](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-hc30).
- **LA and LR:** lanterns. LR models are USB rechargeable. [LA10](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-la10), [LA30](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-la30), [LR10](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-lr10), [LR30](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-lr30).
- **T, TIP, TINI and Tube:** keychain and pocket lights. [TIP 2017](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-tip-2017), [TIP SS](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-tip-ss), [TIP CU](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-tip-cu), [TINI](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-tini), [Tube UV](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-tube-uv), [T5s](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-t5s).
- **E:** explosion-proof rated lights. EF is a torch, EH is a headlamp. [EF1](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-ef1), [EH1S](https://torchoutlet.com.au/products/nitecore-eh1s).

### What GT means

GT is the long-throw version of a model. The MH12 reaches 232 metres. The MH12GT, same size, reaches 320 metres with a tighter beam.

### Are these the latest models?

Much of our range is earlier-generation Nitecore, brand new in sealed packaging. Nitecore updates its models often, so the newest versions may have a different name or charge port. The rechargeable models here charge by micro USB. That is why the prices are what they are.

If you are replacing a torch you already own and love, this is where you find the same one.

# Questions and answers

**Is this genuine Nitecore stock?**
Yes. Every light is a genuine product, brand new in its sealed retail box. When yours arrives, check the model, the serial number and the tags against the box. If anything does not match, send it back for a full refund.

**Why is it about half price?**
Most of our stock is the original version of a model the maker has since updated, and it has been sitting in its boxes on our shelf. We priced it to clear at half the Australian retail price, rounded down to the dollar.

**What does the retail price mean?**
It is the price Australian shops sold that model for when it was on general sale. Where a retailer stated a recommended retail price, we used that. Where we found no Australian retail price, we show our price alone.

**Is the stock new?**
Yes. Everything is brand new in sealed retail packaging, held on the Sunshine Coast in Queensland.

**Are these the latest Nitecore models?**
Much of our range is earlier-generation Nitecore, new in the box. The rechargeable models charge by micro USB. That is why the prices are what they are. If you are replacing a torch you already own, this is where you find the same one.

**Do I need to charge it before I use it?**
Yes. Give any rechargeable light a full charge before you rely on it. A lithium battery that has sat in a box needs topping up.

**Are batteries included?**
It depends on the light. Each product page says what is in the box. Lights with a built-in battery need nothing else. Some torches take 18650, CR123 or AA batteries that you supply.

**How do you ship?**
By road from the Sunshine Coast, Queensland, Australia wide. We send lights with lithium batteries by road freight. Shipping cost shows at checkout before you pay.

**Can I pick up?**
Yes, from the Sunshine Coast by appointment. Call us to arrange it.

**Who am I buying from?**
Torch Outlet is a Coastal Trade Supply brand. Coastal Trade Supply is a trading name of Happy Sisyphus Pty Ltd, Sunshine Coast, Queensland. You pay on the Coastal Trade Supply secure checkout, which runs on Shopify.

**What if something is wrong with my order?**
Call us. Australian Consumer Law guarantees apply to everything we sell. If a light arrives faulty or not as described, we will put it right.

**Will your explosion-proof lights be accepted on my site?**
That is decided by your site, so check first. Many Australian sites require IECEx or ANZEx certification. Call us and we will send a photo of the certification marking on the actual unit before you buy.
